LVKE.|135}}</noinclude>Lord, standing on the right hand of the altar of incense. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=12}}† And Zacharie vvas troubled, seeing him: and feare fel vpon him. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=13}}† But the Angel said to him, Feare not Zacharie, for thy praier is heard: and thy vvife Elizabeth shal beare thee a sonne, and thou shalt cal his name Iohn: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=14}}† and thou shalt haue {{sup|‖}} ioy and exultation, and many shal reioyce in his natiuitie. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=15}}† for he shal be great before our Lord: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This abstinence foretold and prescribed by the Angel, sheweth that it is a worthy thing, and an acte of religion in S. Iohn, as it was in the Nazarites.}}∷ and vvine and sicer he shal not drinke: and he shal be replenished vvith the Holy Ghost euen from his mothers vvombe. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=16}}† and he shal {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 4, 6. Mt. 11, 14.''}}* conuert many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=17}}† and he shal goe before him in the spirit and vertue of Elias: that he may conuert the hartes of the fathers vnto the children, and the incredulous to the vvisedom of the iust, to prepare vnto the Lord a perfect people.⊣ {{verse|chapter=1|verse=18}}† And Zacharie said to the Angel, VVhereby shal I knovv this? for I am old: and my vvife is vvel striken in her daies. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=19}}† And the Angel ansvvering said to him, I am Gabriel that assist before God: and am sent to speake to thee, and to euangelize these things to thee. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=20}}† And behold, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Zacharie punished for doubting of the Angels word.}}∷ thou shalt be dumme, and shalt not be able to speake vntil the day vvherein these things shal be done: for-because thou hast not beleeued my vvordes, vvhich shal be fulfilled in their time. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=21}}† And the people vvas expecting Zacharie: and they marueled that he made tariance in the temple. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=22}}† And comming forth he could not speake to them, and they knevv that he had seen a vision in the temple. And he made signes to them, and remained dumme. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=23}}† And it came to passe, after the daies of his office vvere expired, {{sup|‖}} he departed into his house. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=24}}† And after these daies Elizabeth his vvife conceiued: and hid her self fiue moneths, saying, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=25}}† For thus hath our Lord done to me in the daies vvherein he had respect to take avvay my reproche among men.

{{verse|chapter=1|verse=26}}† b {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Annunciation of our Lady, ''March 25''. And on the wenesday of Imber weeke in Aduent. And for a Votiue Masse of our Lady in Aduent.}}And in the sixt moneth, the Angel Gabriel vvas sent of God into a citie of Galilee, called Nazareth, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=27}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 1, 18.''}}* to a virgin despoused to a man vvhose name vvas Ioseph, of the house of Dauid: and the virgins name vvas {{sc|Marie}}, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=28}}† And the Angel being entred in, said vnto her, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The beginning of the AVE MARIE. See the rest v. 42.}}∷ ''{{sup|‖}} {{sc|Haile}} {{sup|‖}} ful of grace, our Lord is vvith thee: blessed art thou among vvomen''. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=29}}† Vvho hauing heard, vvas troubled at his saying, and thought vvhat maner of salutation this should be. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=30}}† And the Angel said to her, Feare not {{sc|Marie}}, for thou hast found grace vvith God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=31}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 7, 14.''}}* Behold<noinclude>{{rh|||thou}}</noinclude>
